articleTitle: The Full-Cycle Wireline Logging Data Archive System Based on Gopacket
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The ELIS/ESCOOL wireline logging system developed by COSL has achieved excellent results, formed an independent technology system, and made important contributions to offshore oil exploration and development. However, the current wireline logging system still has deficiencies in data integrity and can only store data in recording mode, while data in non-recording mode also has important research value. In response to the needs of oilfield digital transformation, this paper proposes a full-cycle wireline logging data acquisition and integration solution based on network monitoring technology, aiming to generate a full-cycle data archive for wireline logging and provide support for subsequent technical development research. This solution combines the actual production environment and business needs of COSL(China Oilfield Services Limited), and without interfering with the existing logging system, based on Google's open source Gopacket network monitoring library, adopts a producer-consumer model to achieve asynchronous concurrent acquisition. The production end implements TCP stream reassembly and deduplication of data packets, and the consumer end completes the parsing of data protocol packets and logging data caching through concurrent technology. The actual logging test has verified that the full-cycle wireline logging data acquisition program implemented in this paper runs efficiently and has achieved good results, providing strong support for the digital transformation of oilfield logging.

articleTitle: Guiding Grokking: How Curriculum Learning Shapes Algorithmic Understanding in Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Understanding how neural networks suddenly achieve strong generalization after extended training (grokking) remains a fundamental challenge in deep learning. While this phenomenon has been observed in algorithmic tasks, the factors influencing its emergence remain poorly understood. We investigate whether curriculum learning—gradually increasing task complexity—can facilitate and accelerate grokking. Through systematic experiments on modular arithmetic tasks with varying prime moduli, we compare four curriculum strategies (linear, exponential, step-wise, and gradual progression) against a baseline. Our results reveal that only modular addition benefits significantly from curriculum learning, achieving 81.1% validation accuracy with gradual progression compared to 65.7% and 57.2% for linear and exponential curricula respectively. In contrast, operations like modular division and permutation show minimal improvement, with validation accuracies below 20% across all curricula. The gradual curriculum maintains smoother training loss transitions and higher training stability, particularly for addition, while step-wise progression shows the worst performance with validation accuracy drop- ping to 34.4% for addition. These findings suggest curriculum learning is most effective for operations with simpler underlying structures, while complex operations remain challenging regardless of curriculum design. This work provides practical insights into curriculum strategies for algorithmic learning tasks and highlights fundamental limitations of current approaches.

articleTitle: LighterDet: A Lightweight Underwater Object Detection Method Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Underwater optical image object detection plays a crucial role in marine resource exploitation. However, due to limited computational resources in underwater computing devices, existing underwater object detection methods with numerous parameters are not suitable for such scenarios. To address this issue, we propose a new lightweight underwater object detection method based on YOLOv8, which is designed for resource-constrained scenarios. Specifically, we incorporate a lightweight backbone to reduce the detector's computational burden. Additionally, we propose a novel lightweight feature pyramid network that incorporates the depthwise separable convolutions. Extensive experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our method. The experimental results show that our method exceeds the state-of-the-art detector YOLOv8 by 1.8 AP points.

articleTitle: Analysis of Development Paths for Intelligent Sports Education Based on Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: This study analyzes the development paths for intelligent sports education based on artificial intelligence. The article explores four main development paths: the construction of intelligent sports teaching platforms, the development of motion recognition and assessment systems, the creation of virtual reality training environments, and the generation of personalized training programs. The study elaborates on the key technological implementations of these paths, including data collection and preprocessing, application of artificial intelligence algorithms, and edge computing and real-time processing. Through experimental design and validation, the feasibility and effectiveness of these paths are analyzed. The results show that these intelligent development paths can significantly enhance students' skill levels and learning engagement but also face challenges such as high initial investment and substantial teacher training requirements. This research provides a theoretical basis and practical guidance for the intelligent transformation of sports education, which is of great significance for advancing the modernization of sports education.

articleTitle: ARTDet: A Novel Attention-Based Deep Learning Network for Real-Time Head Posture Detection of Students
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Head posture detection of students in classroom environments is crucial for monitoring engagement and optimizing the learning experience. However, this task remains challenging, especially in crowded and dynamic classroom settings where small targets are prevalent. To address this, we propose ARTDet (Attention-based Real-Time Detection for Classroom), a novel network for the detection of the head posture of students based on deep learning. To boost detection performance in classroom environments and address multi-student scenarios, we incorporate the NAM (Normalization-based Attention Module) into the backbone, greatly refining the model's capacity to detect small targets in challenging backgrounds. In addition, we create a custom classroom dataset, manually annotating each student with bounding boxes and posture classifications, providing valuable resources for training and evaluation. Extensive experimental validation demonstrates that ARTDet outperforms existing methods in both quantitative and qualitative assessments.

articleTitle: Application of SAM Model in Zero-shot Segmentation of Skin Wound Images
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Quantitative evaluation of skin wounds is important in tracking the healing process and planning the treatment. For non-invasive and automatic analysis of the wound, segmentation of the wound area from images is a primary step. This study evaluates the performance of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) in the task of segmenting skin wound images. SAM supports zeroshot segmentation, thus eliminating the need to build large training datasets. The adaptability and potential of SAM in this task is fully demonstrated through a variety of different prompting strategies. The results of the study indicate that SAM has a good ability to segment skin wound images and can accurately segment wounds with few prompts. This study provides practical guidance for the clinical application of the SAM model and suggests ways to further optimize the results, ultimately aiming to improve the efficiency and accuracy of skin wound analysis.

articleTitle: A Knowledge-Guided XGBoost Model for Predicting Aluminum Alloy Corrosion Rates in Atmospheric Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Accurate prediction of aluminum alloy corrosion rates in atmospheric environments is crucial for material performance optimization and engineering safety. Traditional data-driven machine learning models often face challenges such as poor robustness and interpretability, especially when dealing with small sample datasets. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Knowledge-Guided XGBoost (KG-XGBoost) model that integrates domain knowledge into the machine learning process. The model incorporates new features, such as work function (WF) and chlorine adsorption energy (CIAE), calculated based on first-principles calculations, and introduces a composite loss function that combines data-driven and physics-based constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that the KG-XGBoost model significantly improves prediction accuracy and robustness compared to traditional XGBoost models.

articleTitle: Research on Detection and Tracking Algorithm for Small and Weak Targets on the Sea Surface Based on Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: To address practical issues such as complex backgrounds, indistinct target features, and poor real-time performance in detecting and tracking small and weak targets at sea, this paper first designs a guided filter algorithm fused with a foggy day imaging model for image preprocessing. This aims to simplify the background complexity. Subsequently, the incremental YOLOv8 detection head algorithm is employed for detecting and tracking these targets, while integrating the ACmix hybrid model to enhance overall operational efficiency. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: Small and Weak Targets at Sea

articleTitle: A 3D Registration Algorithm Based on Mesh and Common Subgraph
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In the fields of computer vision and 3D modeling, Point cloud registration (PCR) plays a crucial role, involving the alignment of multiple point cloud datasets acquired from different perspectives or time points into a common reference coordinate system. It is vital in various applications such as 3D reconstruction, object recognition, and autonomous driving. However, the process of PCR often encounters challenges such as noise interference, partial overlap, and data loss, which significantly impact the accuracy and efficiency of registration. This paper addresses these challenges in PCR by proposing an algorithm that utilizes graph structures. The algorithm converts point clouds into mesh form, which avoids intersecting edges in space, and then filters and removes certain edges based on whether the curvature difference between two points exceeds a set threshold. This ensures that the remaining edges can effectively represent the local edges of the object, thus obtaining a graph representation of the point cloud. Subsequently, for the graphs corresponding to the two point clouds, an optimized graph algorithm is used to search for common subgraphs to determine the correspondence between points in the point clouds, achieving point cloud registration. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to other algorithms, our approach yields satisfactory performance.

articleTitle: A Survey of Physical Adversarial Attacks Against Infrared Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The existence of adversarial examples revealed the underlying vulnerabilities of deep learning models. In the digital domain, meticulously designed subtle perturbations could degrade model performance or even completely cause it to lose its intended functionality. In real-world physical scenarios, adversarial examples also demonstrated potent destructive power and substantial risks. This survey explored the issue of physical adversarial attacks in the crucial field of infrared object detection. Firstly, it provided a clear and in-depth explanation of the concept of physical adversarial attacks in the field of infrared target detection, distinguishing them from traditional digital adversarial attacks, and precisely locating their unique roles and manifestations in real-world scenarios. Secondly, focusing on the diverse detection tasks and targets in infrared scenarios, this review comprehensively and thoroughly examined the emerging physical adversarial attack methods targeting infrared object detection network models, from the perspectives of different detection systems such as pedestrian, vehicle, and remote sensing data detection. Finally, based on the then-current research achievements and technological development trends, it offered a positive outlook for the future of this field.

articleTitle: TSM-YOLO: An Optimized YOLOv11 Model for Traffic State Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: With the increase in traffic flow and the growing complexity of traffic scenes, constructing a precise and efficient traffic state monitor has become a core topic in intelligent transportation. Traffic state monitor involves multi-target recognition, positioning, and status monitoring, which plays a crucial role in aspects such as traffic management. The YOLOv11 model has excellent real-time detection capabilities, but it has limitations when used for traffic state monitor. This paper proposes the TSM-YOLO target detection model, which innovatively optimizes the key aspects of the original YOLOv11 to improve its detection performance in traffic scenes: 1.Regarding the MPDIoU function, The original IoU metric lacks sufficient precision and thus cannot measure the matching degree between the predicted box and the real box, especially in complex situations where traffic targets are occluded. By analyzing the spatial distribution and mutual relationships of traffic targets, this function is improved and penalty mechanism are optimized, the accuracy of target positioning is enhanced, and the detection error is reduced. 2. Given the importance of feature extraction, the SENetV2 algorithm is introduced. Traffic targets are diverse, and traditional feature extraction modules have difficulty adapting to capture key features. However, SENetV2 can adaptively recalibrate feature channels to highlight important features. For example, when distinguishing vehicles, it can strengthen the key feature channels to make classification and positioning more accurate. To verify its effectiveness, a large-scale dataset contain multiple actual traffic scenes, and comparative experiments were carried out after annotation and pre-processing. The results show that compared with the original algorithms model, TSM-YOLO algorithm has a significantly improved average accuracy rate. It can detect key targets more accurately to provide strong support for traffic management and research value.

articleTitle: LIC-PHM: Parameterized Hybrid Module for Learned Image Compression
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Learned image compression has attracted great attention in image and video coding, due to its learnable capabilities and powerful expressiveness. However, the introduction of vision transformer seems to have limited the room for improvement in its coding performance. Inspired by feature representation, convolutional layers (named as CNN) can preserve the locality of image content and vision transformer layer can maintain the global attributes of image, but the latent features of them cannot describe the finer-detailed image content. In this paper, the parameterized hybrid module is proposed to obtain the finer representation of image contours and aggregate the multiple types of feature for efficient image compression. Firstly, we introduce the mixed CNN and Swin Transformer architecture as the base model, integrate the graph-structured Swin Transformer scheme and design a graph-aware edge convolution layer. Secondly, we combine the convolution branch, the two-stage graph-Transformer branch and graph-aware edge convolution branch in parameterized weighing manner to obtain the hierachical features of latent representation. Finally, a noval learned image compression with parameterized hybrid module is trained on 300K images of the OpenImage dataset, and the trained model is tested on Kodak dataset.

articleTitle: CLIF-Adjoint: Accelerating Training of CLIF with Adjoint Method
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Surrogate gradients offer an effective approach for training spiking neural networks (SNNs), allowing them to achieve classification results comparable to those of artificial neural networks. Recent research has highlighted the enhanced performance of spiking neurons, particularly CLIF and similar types. However, the high cost of training these new neurons with surrogate gradient methods limits their efficiency. In this work, we introduce CLIF-adjoint neurons and utilize the adjoint method to speed up the training process. We measured the CLIF-adjoint neurons on multiple classification tasks, including static datasets and neuromorphic datasets. Our experiments demonstrated that using CLIF-adjoint neurons can significantly reduce the training time of SNNs while achieving classification accuracy that matches the original neurons. Additionally, with time steps 20, the training speed was improved by 2.05 times with CLIF-adjoint neurons.

articleTitle: The Development Trend Analysis of Pet Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In this paper, we study the pet industry of China. Firstly, we analyze the factors in the development of China's pet industry based on the data and apply some regressions to select features. Furthermore, we combine the random forest and polynomial regression model to construct a hybrid algorithm to predict the development trend of pet food industry. Then we use the Analytic Hierarchy Process(AHP)-Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution(TOPSIS) to evaluate of the market and get the score for China's pet food industry so that we can get a more comprehensive and precise evaluation. What's more, we build a hybrid algorithm to predict pet food industry of China. At last, we analyze the development of the global pet industry and give some suggestions to the pet industry.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Low-Light Image Enhancement Based on Light Effect Region Suppression
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Aiming at the coupling problem of light effect interference and non-linear degradation in low-light images, this paper proposes a double-stage enhancement framework integrating hierarchical illumination decomposition and adversarial training. In order to avoid the overcorrection phenomenon of traditional enhancement methods to the light effect area, a light sensitive network is constructed to decouple the reconstruction of the illumination and reflection layers. And, a dynamic exposure regulation module is designed to learn the brightness mapping function of local regions implicit neural representation. Then, the local adaptive gamma correction is performed. Furthermore, a multi-scale adaptive transformer architecture is proposed, which adopts a deformable window mechanism to achieve long-range dependency modeling, to enhance the recovery ability of local degradation features through gate convolutional. In addition, the adversarial co-training strategy is introduced to guide the model to generate results that meet the physical light distribution by jointly using multi-scale discriminators and spectral constraint losses. Experimental results show that the proposed method, which can achieve balanced enhancement in dark areas, leads in SSIM indicators and most of PSNR is optimal.

articleTitle: LitRank: An Interactive Tool for Ranking and Field Inference in Literary Data
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Advancements in digital humanities have enabled new approaches to analyzing literary works. However, challenges arise in managing fragmented historical records, complex relationships, and multidimensional data, including timelines, locations, and interpersonal connections. This paper introduces LitRank, a visualization tool designed to explore 431 historical Chinese collections. LitRank evaluates the literary impact of collections and writers using role-based author contributions and defined metrics like authorship, commentary mentions, and biographical records. It also helps experts focus on addressing critical data gaps by identifying records with high literary impact and significant missing fields. Furthermore, LitRank infers missing temporal details and uncovers potential kinships among co-authors by analyzing shared surnames and collaboration patterns, providing deeper insights into the literary corpus.

articleTitle: RSIAW: A Robust and Inconspicuous Watermarking Framework for Remote Sensing Images Using Adversarial Perturbations and Style Transfer
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Remote sensing imagery is crucial for applications such as urban planning, resource management, and defense, yet it is increasingly vulnerable to data theft and tampering. Traditional protection methods, such as encryption and access control, are limited, especially with the rise of deep neural networks that can effectively remove visible watermarks. This paper presents RSIAW, a watermarking technique that combines adversarial perturbations and style transfer to enhance robustness and authenticity. Adversarial perturbations mislead watermark removal models, while style transfer improves visual coherence by integrating the watermark with the image texture. Evaluated on the NWPU-RESISC45 dataset, RSIAW demonstrates strong resistance to removal attacks while preserving image usability. The method's performance is assessed using Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), yielding a PSNR of 0.984, SSIM of 42.59, and RMSE of 2.24, indicating high similarity and quality between the watermarked and original images. RSIAW outperforms baseline methods in resistance to removal attacks, achieving the highest SSIM (0.996) and PSNR (49.04) values with a watermark size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40\times 40$</tex> and opacity of 0.4.

articleTitle: YOLO-ASFF: A Model for Detecting Tomatoes of Different Maturities Based on Improved YOLO v5s
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In agricultural production, accurate detection of tomatoes of different maturities is crucial to control the picking time and improve grading efficiency. However, the orchard environment is complex, which brings many challenges to detecting tomatoes of different maturities, such as variable light conditions, lush branches and leaves, fruit occlusion, tomatoes with different sizes, etc. Traditional methods rely on manual experience, which is not only time-consuming but also has limited accuracy. To this end, the YOLO-ASFF model is proposed to improve the detection accuracy of tomatoes of different maturities in complex orchard environments in this work. On the one hand, the model uses the extended intersection over union (EIoU) to optimize the bounding box positioning to ensure that tomatoes of different sizes and maturities could be accurately framed. On the other hand, the adaptive spatial feature fusion (ASFF) module was integrated to enhance the fusion ability of multi-scale features, so that the model could capture feature information more comprehensively when detecting tomatoes with different maturities. The experimental results show that the YOLO-ASFF model performs better than other models, including Faster R-CNN, EfficientNet, YOLO v5s, and YOLO v11n, in detecting tomatoes of different maturities, with an accuracy of 0.885, a recall rate of 0.835, a mean average precision of 0.850, and an Fl-Score of 0.850. In short, YOLO-ASFF can provide an effective method for accurately identifying tomatoes with different maturities, which can help reduce labor costs and improve picking efficiency.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Image Segmentation Based on Bi-Directional Cascade Network
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Image segmentation is the way of splitting digital data into subgroups known as image segments, which reduces the entire image's complexity and allows for further processing or image analysis of each segment. The general segmentation techniques of images are divided into traditional methods and deep learning methods. In this paper, we introduce a deep-learning approach to a traditional image segmentation method (i.e., edge detection) and propose a new framework for hierarchical image segmentation. In the new framework, we first use the Bi-Directional Cascade Network (BDCN) model as our edge detector to preprocess the input image in order to form a feature map with coarse edges. Then, we refine the edges of the image by using the watershed algorithm. Finally, we form a segmentation dendrogram by using the Ultrametric Contour Map (UCM) algorithm. Extensive experiments have demonstrated that our proposed framework has significant advantages in segmentation performance compared to the state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: An Efficient Data Synchronization Tool Design and Implementation Based on Data Flow
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In the digital transformation of equipment development, there is an increasing demand for data synchronization. Traditional data synchronization schemes generally face reliability deficiencies and real-time bottlenecks, making it difficult to meet enterprise requirements for real-time synchronization of massive data. This paper introduces an efficient data synchronization tool based on data flow, aiming to address the shortcomings of traditional data synchronization methods. The tool adopts publish-subscribe pattern to build the data transmission architecture, and through the double-ended asynchronous queues to achieve decoupled communication mechanism, thus allowing one-to-many data synchronization. In the database synchronization layer, it innovatively adopts the data flow direct connection technology to replace the traditional SQL statement parsing, and achieves efficient synchronization of largescale data through zero middleware writing and batch streaming processing technology. This paper details the technical architecture and implementation of the tool, and verifies its superior performance in large-scale data synchronization scenarios through experiments. Experimental results show that the tool significantly outperforms traditional methods in terms of synchronization efficiency, and the synchronization latency of ten million data volumes can be controlled at the second level. Compared with the widely used data synchronization tool NIFI, our tool exhibits superior data synchronization performance in large-scale data synchronization scenarios, providing a new solution for high-efficiency data synchronization between databases.

articleTitle: A Soft Body Actuator Position Measurement Method Based on OpenCV Library
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The inherent deformability of soft body robots renders the conventional rigid measurement techniques inapplicable to the assessment of their structural integrity. Consequently, the investigation of appropriate measurement methodologies for soft body structures has emerged as a prominent area of research. This paper proposes a visual processing algorithm based on the OpenCV library for the measurement of the position of soft robots. By affixing a defined number of marker points to the soft body robot, the bending contour can be extracted with precision and efficiency through the recognition of the marker points and the subsequent extraction of the overall contour. This method requires a minimal number of marker points and the algorithm is highly efficient. The location of the marker points is not a strict requirement, and the method is highly practical as it can be applied to the position measurement of a wide range of soft-body robots with varying structures. This research provides a valuable reference for the field of soft-body measurement.

articleTitle: DISO-DETR: A Detail-Enhanced Infrared Small Object Detection Transformer Based on UAV Imagery
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: When it comes to detecting small objects in infrared images using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), existing models really struggle with a few big obstacles. The tiny size of the targets, the cluttered backgrounds, and the need to run efficiently on edge devices all present major challenges. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel detail-enhanced infrared small object detection model, DISO-DETR, based on the RT-DETR architecture. It introduces two key innovations: the Multiscale Detail Feature Backbone Network and the Wavelet-based Frequency Feather Aggregation module. These two modules effectively boost the model to capitalize on the infrared image details while maintaining a lightweight design. This makes it a great fit for real-time use on edge devices. Experimental validation shows that the mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf> of DISO-DETR is raised by 6%, and the number of parameters and Gflops are reduced by 21.6% and 22.6%, respectively, over the base model on the HIT-UAV dataset. Moreover, when compared to other advanced models, DISO-DETR not only improves infrared small target detection performance but also demonstrates superior efficiency and robustness, proving its advantages in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Model for Anomaly Detection in Reducing Water Losses in the Distribution Network of Peru using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Water leakage in distribution networks is a significant challenge, especially in regions with limited infrastructure like Huancayo, Peru, where losses account for 32.82% of the distributed volume. This study introduces a machine learning-based approach to detect leaks using four algorithms: Autoencoder LSTM, Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). The methodology involved preprocessing historical consumption data (2018–2024) into 12-month temporal sequences per client and evaluating the models based on F1 Score, Precision, and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Among the algorithms, the Autoencoder LSTM demonstrated superior performance with the highest precision (0.89) and the lowest MAE (0.00402). Its robustness in high-variability contexts enables early and reliable leak detection, providing a cost-effective solution for optimizing water management in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Research on Deep Learning Network Sample Generation Method Based on Abnormal Examples
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The complexity and uncertainty of deep neural networks (DNN) necessitate comprehensive behavior testing for model quality assurance. Current studies generating samples via coverage criteria and fuzz testing often neglect sample diversity and error-detection ability. The surprise adequacy metric, quantifying neuron output differences between samples and the training set, lacks a specific generation method. Herein, a novel method is introduced. Initially, key decision-influencing neurons are identified to refine the surprise adequacy metric. Subsequently, seed samples with error-revealing potential are filtered by this metric. Finally, integrating coverage-guided fuzz testing, with the surprise adequacy value and class probability difference as joint optimization targets, the gradient ascent algorithm computes perturbations for iterative sample generation. Five DNN models and four image datasets were used for validation. Results confirm that the enhanced metric swiftly captures abnormal samples and saves computation time. In sample generation, compared to DeepGini and RobOT, the derived test sets' surprise coverage rises by up to 5.9% and 15.9% respectively; versus DLFuzz and DeepXplore, the proposed method achieves a boost of up to 26.5% and 33.7%, validating its efficacy.

articleTitle: Path Optimization Model for Tandem Rectangular Rigid Bodies Based on Spiral Paths
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: With the increasing demand for the application of path planning in motion control of complex systems, how to design efficient and safe paths in limited space has become an important research topic. The article takes the Bench Dragon dance team as the research object, combines its motion path characteristics, and constructs a spiral path optimization model, which provides a theoretical reference for the path planning problem of tandem rectangular rigid body system. Firstly, based on the geometrical characteristics of the screw thread, the pitch optimization model is established, and the key parameters to avoid collision are analyzed through the separation axis theorem; Secondly, based on the actual data, the optimization model of the turnaround path is constructed, and the space utilization rate and motion safety of the turnaround path are optimized through the path characteristics of the two tangent circular arcs; Lastly, the reasonableness of the constructed model is analyzed in combination with the actual problems, and the validity and practical value of the optimized path is verified. The constructed model has high application value, effectively avoids collision in the process of movement, improves the efficiency of path design and safety of movement, and can provide scientific basis for the path optimization of complex tandem rigid body system in practical engineering.

articleTitle: Empowering Software Architects with Artificial Intelligence: Analyzing GitHub Copilot's Role in Modern Architecture Design
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: As artificial intelligence tools like GitHub Copilot become more integrated into software development workflows, they are transforming how architects approach modern software design. Although enterprises are exploring the potential of GenAl tools to improve developer productivity, limited research exists on their impact on the role of software architects. Traditionally, architects use various tools to create architectural blueprints, including Unified Modeling Language (UML) diagrams, class diagrams, sequence diagrams, use case diagrams, component diagrams, deployment diagrams, activity diagrams, and state diagrams, to name a few. Many of these diagrams follow repetitive patterns that could be automated with well-defined contexts. This paper examines Copilot's role in supporting architects through various stages of architectural development, evaluating how closely Copilot-generated outputs align with established architectural principles. By analyzing deviations, the study discusses how refined prompts can yield more accurate results. This research ultimately seeks to determine Copilot's potential to enhance productivity, ensure consistency, and support architectural decision-making, while offering insights into best practices for integrating AI into modern software architecture.

articleTitle: Multi-Intent Enhanced Hypergraph Model for Session-Based Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Session-based recommendation leverages interaction data from anonymous users to suggest items of potential interest. Although existing research typically examines user intent from global and local perspectives, the omission of initial user intent has led to an incomplete understanding of user preferences. Furthermore, during the intent fusion stage, many methods simply sum or concatenate different intents, making it difficult to discriminate the contribution of each intent to the final recommendation. To overcome these limitations, we propose the multi-intent enhanced hypergraph model for session-based recommendation (MEHM). Specifically, we introduce two novel modules: an Initial Intent Learning Module (IILM) and a Multi-Intent Fusion Module (MIFM). In the Initial Intent Learning Module, we propose a first-item-guided strategy that infers the user's initial intent based on the first few items in the session. In the Multi-Intent Fusion Module, we integrate multiple forms of user intent-namely, the initial, global, and current intents-by using global intent as a reference and assigning appropriate weights to both initial and current intents. This design allows for a more precise and holistic representation of user preferences. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: MSCANet: A Multi-Scale Separable Convolution Attention Network for Cephalometric Landmark Detection in X-Ray Images
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Cephalometric landmark detection in lateral X-rays plays a crucial role in orthodontic treatment, craniofacial growth research, and surgical planning. Traditional manual annotation methods are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and prone to errors. Aiming at these problems, we propose MSCANet, an advanced encoder-decoder framework that leverages multi-scale separable convolution and attention mechanisms to enhance the precision and robustness of cephalometric landmark detection. Specifically, MSCANet integrates three key components: the Multi-Scale Separable Convolution Block (MSCB) for extracting multi-scale features without increasing the parameter count, the Pyramid Skip Feature Fusion (PSFF) module for integrating global features of different sizes with the local feature, and the Enhanced Squeeze-and-Excitation (ESE) module to recalibrate feature maps and emphasize relevant spatial features. These components enable MSCANet to accurately capture both global and local structural details, improving landmark localization in complex scenarios. Experimental results on the public ISBI 2015 dataset show that MSCANet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving significant reductions in mean radial error (MRE) and improved success detection rates (SDR). These results demonstrate the effectiveness of MSCANet in addressing the limitations of existing approaches and underscore the potential of deep learning techniques for automated medical image analysis tasks, particularly in cephalometric X-rays.

articleTitle: Small Object Detection of Human Face Melasma Based on Improved YOLOv5s
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that YOLOv5s is used for human face melasma detection because it ignores the detail information leading to the missed detection of small objects of the melasma, this paper presents a small object detection method utilizing an optimized version of YOLOv5s. The YOLOv5s-CCB deep learning network is constructed, and the CA attention is integrated into the C3 module of the backbone network to improve the network's capability in capturing the precise location information of small objects; the CARAFE up-sampling module is incorporated through the neck to enhance the model's ability to extract global features; and the BiFPN bi-directional feature pyramid network is introduced during the feature fusion stage, the goal is to effectively combine shallow and deep features. Experimental tests demonstrate that the mAP_0.5 and R of this method are improved by 3.1 % and 3% respectively, the performance surpasses that of the original YOLOv5s detection method.

articleTitle: Region Proposal Exploration for Extending Perspective Detection to Panoramic Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Since panoramic images provide a wide field of view of the surrounding environment, they offer a rich source of information that is increasingly utilized in fields like robotics and autonomous systems. With the application of 360° cameras (i.e. panorama, omnidirectional cameras), robots are gaining 360°perception, enabling them to better understand and interact with their surroundings. However, the unique characteristics of panoramic images, such as geometric distortion and spatial discontinuity introduced by the panoramic projection, pose significant challenges for the application of conventional object detection methods, which are typically designed for perspective images. To address these challenges, current approaches often rely on repetitive overlapping detections to avoid object fragmentation caused by view cuts, but this leads to detection failures and inefficiencies. In this paper, we propose a novel method that explores region proposals within panoramic images to perform view projection. By reducing redundant detections, our approach improves detection efficiency and accuracy. We demonstrate through experiments that our method enhances object detection performance, providing a more effective solution for panoramic image object detection tasks in robotics and autonomous systems.

articleTitle: AdaptiveBufferedThreadPool: An Rejection-Resistant Buffered Thread Pool for Efficient I/O Task Handling
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Existing thread pools struggle with I/O-intensive tasks: the JDK pool underutilizes CPUs due to blocking, while Tomcat wastes resources via excessive thread creation. Both frequently trigger rejection policies under high loads, risking system stability. This paper presents AdaptiveBufferedThreadPool, featuring (1) Buffer-first Rapid Thread Expansion Strategy allows users to suppress excessive thread creation based on business requirements. and (2) Load-Driven Forced Queueing Model to minimize rejections. Experiments demonstrate that compared with Tomcat pool and JDK pool, AdaptiveBufferedThreadPool has higher flexibility in expanding the number of threads to curb over-creation and can achieve a task success rate of over 95% under peak load.

articleTitle: Sparse-View CT Reconstruction Based on Dual-Domain Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is an important medical imaging technique widely used in clinical diagnosis. Sparse-view CT is an effective technique for significantly reducing radiation doses in CT imaging, but it often results in severe artifacts when using traditional reconstruction algorithms such as filtered backprojection (FBP). To address this, we propose a dual-domain deep learning architecture for sparse-view CT reconstruction that reduces radiation dose while enhancing image quality. Based on the U-Net model, this method integrates image domain and sinogram domain information through an improved Domain Fusion Module (DFM), which allows early fusion of these features to tackle blurring and artifacts caused by sparse views. Unlike existing methods, we only extract a portion of features for dual-domain fusion while retaining some original features, balancing fusion and information retention. We also employ a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) in the DFM to prioritize relevant features and improve reconstruction quality. Experiments conducted on the publicly available Mayo2016 dataset demonstrate that our proposed model achieves superior reconstruction quality compared to other state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Multi-Channel Feature Fusion Extraction Method Based on Wavelet Packet in Plant Diseases' Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: To improve the accuracy of plant disease identification, on the basis of wavelet packet image and YUV color space, multi-channel feature fusion extraction algorithm has been proposed. Firstly, the input image is converted into the Y, U, V channels sub-graph, respectively. Then the fusion features based on wavelet packet energy, the Y, U and V-component images are calculated and as the inputs of disease image recognition model. Finally, we compare several wavelet basis, wavelet decomposition levels, color models and feature extraction methods to verify the robustness of our algorithm. The experimental results show that when the particle swarm optimization support vector machine (PSO-SVM) and the ‘haar’-based 2-level wavelet packet decomposition are used, the highest average F1 score is 0.963. Compared with the feature extraction method based on wavelet transforming, the average Fl score of the proposed approach is improved by 0.277.

articleTitle: Algorithmic and Machine Learning Methods for Witten Genus Vanishing Theorems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Witten genus, a fundamental invariant in index theory, extends <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>-genus and plays a crucial role in differential topology and mathematical physics. A central problem concerns identifying conditions under which the Witten genus vanishes, with the Stolz conjecture proposing a connection to positive Ricci curvature. While classical vanishing results exist for specific classes of complete intersections, there is no systematic computational approach for generating and analyzing such manifolds. This work introduces an algorithmic framework for studying the vanishing properties of the Witten genus in string complete intersections. By encoding complete intersections as configuration matrices, we develop an efficient algorithm for generating string manifolds in direct products of projective spaces and Bott manifolds and computing their (mod 2) Witten genera as q-series. As an application, we implement a predictive model using a convolutional neural network, achieving 0.9757 accuracy. CNN consistently outperforms logistic regression, random forests, and XGBoost across most training ratios, demonstrating that structural patterns associated with vanishing behavior can be effectively captured through machine learning.

articleTitle: LLM-Based Teacher Tone Recognition for Educational Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Tone recognition plays a crucial role in E-education, enabling virtual teachers to enhance interactive experiences, provide personalized teaching, and flexibly s imulate diverse teaching styles, thus creating emotionally supportive learning environments. However, existing tone recognition research primarily focuses on general conversational contexts, overlooking the unique and fine-grained t one c haracteristics s pecific to educational settings. Educational tones, such as encouraging, guiding, critical, and neutral tones, are significantly m ore nuanced and differ markedly from everyday conversational tones. To address this gap, this study proposes a LLM-based teacher tone recognition method optimized for educational scenarios. Leveraging the strengths of large language models (LLMs) in language understanding and context analysis, we develop a teacher tone recognition method that processes and analyzes authentic classroom data to accurately classify various tone features. Experiments on 409 classroom utterances using four LLMs show that DeepSeek-V3 achieved the highest accuracy in teacher tone classification, with explicit task prompts significantly improving recognition performance.

articleTitle: A Stylistic Comparative Study for Evaluating Neural Machine Translation Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Neural network-based online machine translation technologies have brought great convenience to foreign language teaching and research. However, performance evaluation of these translation technology models from the perspective of stylistic comparisons are currently scarce. In this study, Wenxin 4.0, DeepSeek-V3, and ChatGPT are used to translate a selection from an ancient Chinese story, and a stylistic comparison is conducted among the three versions of translation. By analyzing the transitivity processes of the original text, along with the three translated versions, it is found that the translations processed by the three technological models are closely similar to the original text in terms of the number and type distribution of transitivity processes. Nevertheless, there were certain differences in the use of mental and behavioral processes compared to the original text. Comparing the semantic configuration, as well as the stylistic feature distributions of the translated versions and the original text, is conducive to examining the differences in existing online translation technology models, both at home and abroad, when handling document-level translation units. This provides a basis for performance evaluation to support technological updates.

articleTitle: Integrated Sensory Platform: Driving Information Sharing in Multi-Level Autonomous Driving Mixed Traffic Mode
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: This article presents an innovative integrated solution called the Integrated Sensory Platform which combines driver and passenger behavior monitoring, vehicle blind spot detection, and V2X communication technology, all aimed at reducing traffic accidents in mixed-traffic scenarios involving multiple levels of automated driving. In this approach, deep learning visual AI technology is employed to identify the types of behaviors of occupants within the cabin, as well as the types of targets detected in blind spots. A three-branch algorithm framework is proposed, which enhances posture and temporal feature extraction, reduces the model's dependence on detailed features, and strengthens its ability to resist occlusion. Additionally, an expanded group channel reordering mechanism is designed to optimize the classification and recognition performance of the posture and temporal feature branches. The identified information is then broadcasted to surrounding vehicles via V2X communication, enabling deep information sharing among multiple vehicles in a spatial traffic environment. This information not only provides decision-making data for high-level automated driving vehicles but also offers operational guidance for fully human-driven vehicles, achieving the goal of collaborative decision-making among vehicles of varying automation levels and improving road traffic safety in complex mixed-traffic conditions.

articleTitle: Multi Sensor Data Fusion Algorithm Based on Multi Neural Network Decision Model and D-S Evidence Theory
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: A data fusion model TFIT-DS based on multi neural network decision model and D-S evidence is proposed to address the uncertainty and redundancy of sensor data. This model utilizes the D-S evidence theory to fuse the decision information output from the attention based Transformer model and the InceptionTime model with convolutional neural network structure at the decision level. Through the depth combination structure, the model can fully perceive the characteristics of sensor data in different situations, thus achieving a new breakthrough on the basis of high-precision based on a single mode. According to the experimental outcomes, the model is able to effectively fuse different sensor information and has high accuracy in bearing fault identification.

articleTitle: MBAug: Metamorphic BERT-Based Augmentation for Improving Deep Learning-Based Fault Localization Without Test Oracles
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Deep Learning-based Fault Localization (DLFL) uses metamorphic testing to locate faults in the absence of test oracles. However, these approaches often face the issue of class imbalance, where the violated data (minority class) is significantly less than the non-violated data (majority class). To address this challenge, we propose MBAug: Metamorphic Bert-based Augmentation for improving DLFL without test oracles. MBAug combines metamorphic testing and BERT to generate the data of minority class and acquire class balanced data. We apply MBAug to two state-of-the-art DLFL baselines without test oracles, and the results show that MBAug significantly outperforms all the baselines in the absence of test oracles. This work provides a generalizable solution for class imbalance challenges in test oracle-free scenarios, advancing intelligent software engineering practices.

articleTitle: Model for Endometriosis Detection Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic disease that affects a considerable percentage of women of reproductive age and is characterized by the presence of endometrial tissue outside the uterine cavity, leading to symptoms such as pelvic pain and dysmenorrhea. The aim of this study is to develop a predictive model for the classification of endometriosis using four Machine Learning algorithms: Random Forest, LASSO, SVM, and Naive Bayes. For this purpose, a dataset from the Global Health Data Exchange was utilized, consisting of 1,000 cases of patients with endometriosis. The methodology included data cleaning and preprocessing, as well as the evaluation of each algorithm's performance using four metrics: precision, recall, F1-Score, and accuracy. The findings revealed that the Random Forest algorithm was the most effective in identifying endometriosis, outperforming the other algorithms with a precision of 0.99 for the “endometriosis” class and an overall accuracy of 0.98.

articleTitle: Galactic Wandering: An Immersive Tour of the Solar System
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In recent years, the integration of innovative tech-nologies in education has become increasingly important to enhance student engagement and learning outcomes, particularly in specialized fields such as astronomy. Traditional teaching tools, such as PowerPoint slides and videos, often lack interactivity and immersion. To address these challenges, we conducted a user survey that revealed a strong demand for immersive educational experiences, prompting us to prioritize user-centered design. Therefore, we developed an immersive teaching application for the solar system based on virtual reality (VR). This application allows users to explore the solar system immersively, observe planetary surface and their satellites up close, experience astro-nomical phenomena like solar and lunar eclipses, and examine planetary topography from various perspectives. The application was used by participants in an astronomy exhibition in a university museum, where questionnaires and verbal feedback were collected. Results indicated that the flexible interactivity and immersive experience appeal to a lot of engagement participants. This study highlights the practical application of virtual reality in teaching and the dissemination of astronomy, and its potential to foster scientific curiosity and deepen students' understanding of astronomy.

articleTitle: An Expectation-Based Dynamically Adjusted Gossip Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The Gossip algorithm is a decentralized commu-nication algorithm primarily used to address information dis-semination and consistency issues in distributed systems. The Gossip protocol, with its significant distributed characteristics and advantages, has been widely applied in critical domains such as fault detection, resource allocation, global search, and robot operating system node communication. However, compared to traditional non-decentralized algorithms, the Gossip algorithm tends to generate more message redundancy during the infor-mation dissemination process, which to some extent impacts its communication efficiency. To address this issue, we propose a universal expectation-based dynamically adjusted Gossip op-timization algorithm that optimizes the message redundancy in the Gossip algorithm during the information dissemination process. This method effectively controls message redundancy by dynamically adjusting the number of message forwarding, denoted as K, in the Gossip algorithm. The experimental results show that in the three scenarios we compared, the message redundancy was reduced by 16.40% to 46.06%, and the original characteristics of the Gossip algorithm were not compromised. The code and experimental results in the paper are all open source.

articleTitle: Super-Resolving X-Ray Security Images with Variational Autoencoder for Prohibited Item Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Most existing super-resolution methods are designed for natural visible light images, relying on subjective visual perception and objective image quality metrics to evaluate their performance. This paper introduces a super-resolution network model, XSR-VAE, specifically designed for pseudo-color X-ray security inspection images. XSR-VAE consists of three main components: Feature Extraction, channel-attention adaptive instance normalization (CAdaIN), and Upsample OneStep. Specifically, the variational autoencoder architecture is employed to construct the prior and posterior distributions of the input. The novel channel-attention adaptive instance normalization is designed to enhance details related to the color and contrast of X-ray security images. Additionally, the denoising function is integrated into the super-resolution process. We conduct experiments on three tasks: image contrast enhancement, image denoising, and image super-resolution. Furthermore, we evaluate the performance of the super-resolution X-ray security images generated by XSR-VAE in detection tasks. The experimental results demonstrate that XSR-VAE effectively enhances image contrast, removes noise, and improves the detection accuracy of prohibited items in object detection tasks.

articleTitle: LLM-Driven Automatic Knowledge Transfer for Promoting Organizational Software Upcycling
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Software upcycling is a methodology aimed at improving the efficiency of the software development process by reusing existing software resources. Previous research introduced the SUCCEED system, which allows development organizations to share upcycling achievements manually as cases. This study proposes an automated knowledge transfer method that leverages large language models (LLMs) for data transformation and filtering, enabling the integration of external community development insights into internal organizational practices as upcycling cases. The proposed method is implemented and evaluated using Stack Overflow. The results demonstrate that LLMs enable accurate transformation of case data, and the proposed filtering approach effectively integrates external knowledge into internal organizational contexts.

articleTitle: Mining More Inter-Cluster Association Information to Improve Ensemble Clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Ensemble clustering has gained increasing attention for its critical role in data analysis. Recent studies emphasize the importance of mining inter-cluster relationships instead of relying solely on pairwise similarities. However, existing methods often fail to fully exploit the global structure of inter-cluster association graphs, limiting their effectiveness. To address this, we propose a Deep Walk-based method to mine and utilize inter-cluster association information more effectively. By learning embeddings of cluster nodes, the approach captures multi-scale and global inter-cluster relationships, which are then incorporated into the co-association matrix to enhance clustering performance. Furthermore, we introduce an adaptive linkage selection strategy for hierarchical clustering as the consensus function. Unlike existing methods with fixed linkage modes, our approach leverages the inter-cluster association graph to adaptively select the most suitable linkage strategy, improving adaptability across diverse datasets. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves superior performance and robustness, validating its effectiveness in ensemble clustering.

articleTitle: MetaPri: Test Input Prioritization Based on Metamorphic Testing
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Owing to the extensive application of deep neural networks (DNNs) in safety-critical tasks, it is necessary to thoroughly test DNN models before model deployment to mitigate risks. However, this typically requires expensive manual labeling and validation, with test cases inputting DNNs to discover erroneous decisions. To address the issues of testing efficiency and testing label costs, previous research has used a prioritization testing approach based on neuron coverage, but such a method proves ineffective in the context of test case prioritization. Other researchers have also attempted mutation-based approaches, but this method is associated with high time costs and low efficiency. To address these shortcomings, in this paper, we propose a DNNs test input prioritization method based on a metamorphosis test called MetaPri. By utilizing a novel diversity metric based on the internal neuron gradients of DNNs, MetaPri mitigates the cost of manual labeling and detects violations. We evaluate the proposed method based on effectiveness, guidance. Experimental results show that MetaPri improves the model accuracy by an average of 9.92% under different confrontation scenarios, which significantly outperforms other baseline methods, as well as verifies its versatility and effectiveness.

articleTitle: RDTD: Adversarial Input Detector Using Reverse Diffusion Transformation
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved performance beyond humans in visual recognition tasks. However, DNNs are susceptible to adversarial examples spoofing, where an attacker adds malicious perturbations to an image causing the neural network to output incorrect results, and this attack often has a high degree of similarity to the original image at the visual level. This paper proposes a reverse diffusion transform detector(RDTD) to defend against such malicious input. We have conducted extensive experiments on MNIST, CIFAR10, and ImageNet datasets using different models, and the results show that our proposed detection framework is effective in detecting adversarial attacks due to the existing defenses. and also shows that our detection framework has better adaptability. Previous defense frameworks do not consider the effectiveness shown in the face of novel digital attacks proposed in recent years. We evaluate the detection effectiveness of the proposed framework in producing adversarial samples from a data distribution perspective, showing that our approach still has high performance in the face of advanced attacks, and demonstrating that our proposed framework can still provide effective defense for deep neural networks against novel attacks.

articleTitle: SenseFS: Enhancing Metadata Efficiency via Adaptive Placement in Disaggregated Persistent Memory
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Distributed File Systems (DFSs) form the backbone of modern data centers' storage infrastructures, with metadata services critical to their performance. The recent emergence of the Disaggregated Persistent Memory (DPM) architecture, which decouples compute and persistent memory resources to enhance hardware utilization, presents an opportunity to innovate meta-data services. However, building a metadata service on the DPM architecture poses two major challenges: (1) numerous small remote reads saturate the lOPS capacity of RDMA Network Interface Cards (RNICs), and (2) frequent cache misses incur high latency penalties. Existing solutions fail to address the above challenges, making it impossible to fully utilize the DPM architecture to improve metadata service performance. This paper presents SenseFS, a metadata service tailored for the DPM architecture, It addresses these challenges with three key designs: (1) organizing metadata into fixed-size locality-preserving metadata buckets (MDBs) to enable efficient access with fewer remote reads, (2) mining the metadata correlation to optimize metadata placement, and (3) adopting a learning-based approach to allocate MDB space based on access patterns to improve space utilization. Evaluation results demonstrate that SenseFS significantly enhances metadata efficiency, achieving higher throughput and reduced latency compared to state-of-the-art solutions.

articleTitle: Energy-Saving System for Wireless Networks: A Time-Series-Based and Neural Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent energy-saving system that utilizes advanced time-series forecasting and neural network optimization to tackle the high energy consumption and increasing operational costs of 2G, 3G, and 4G wireless base stations. The system first employs an Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model to accurately forecast base station load trends. Based on these forecasts, a dynamic energy-saving strategy is developed, incorporating PRB threshold optimization, adaptive resource deactivation, and feedback-driven threshold adjustment. Additionally, a neural network-driven control mechanism is introduced to dynamically refine threshold settings, ensuring energy efficiency without sacrificing network performance. Experimental results from real-world deployments demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves nearly a 9% reduction in power consumption, significantly exceeding traditional energy-saving methods. The system's adaptive iteration further enhances energy efficiency over time, making it a robust solution for the sustainability of future wireless networks.

articleTitle: A Three-Stage Guided Learning Occluded Face Restoration Scheme Based on GAN
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Facial recognition systems often face challenges with partial occlusions, which hinder feature identification and degrade model performance. Although GAN-based methods have shown promise, their reliance on synthetic datasets limits real-world applicability due to the lack of dataset realism. In this paper, we propose a novel three-stage framework that uses occlusion region prediction, facial component segmentation, and face restoration based on the outputs from the initial stages. This approach effectively handles diverse occlusions and bridges the gap between synthetic and real-world scenarios. Experimental results show the superiority of our method, achieving over 91 % on a similarity measure and outperforming existing methods.

articleTitle: Predicting Execution Time for Move Method Refactoring Base on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Move method refactoring (MMR) is one of the most commonly used software maintenance techniques to improve feature envy. Existing work focuses on how to identify and recommend MMR. However, little is known about how MMR impacts program performance. There is a gap between MMR and its impact on performance. To reduce this gap, this paper proposes a novel approach to predict MMR performance based on deep learning and feature interaction. Firstly, construction of the first dataset in this domain. Secondly, FMPerf is built by combining Factor Machine and DeepPerf. Finally, We evaluate FMPerf on real-world projects including JUnit, LC-problems, and Kevin. The experimental results show that FMPerf obtains an average of 7.31 % MRE, illustrating that the predicted value is close to the real value. Furthermore, FMPerf improves MRE ranging from 2.29 % to 11.02 % compared to existing approaches, including Convolutional Neural Networks(CNN), Factorization-Machine based Neural Network(DeepFM), Performance Prediction with Deep Sparse Neural Network(DeepPerf), and Hierarchical Inter-action Neural Network for Performance Prediction(HINNPerf), demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: OntoSce: Domain-Oriented FTA Analysis for Generating Safety-Critical Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The widespread application of autonomous driving technology has triggered in-depth discussions on its safety and reliability. To address this challenge, this paper presents the safety-critical scenario generation tool OntoSce, which is driven by a domain model and integrates Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) for causal analysis, enabling the automated generation of safety-critical scenarios. The research first explores domain-oriented FTA analysis, elaborating on two dimensions: traffic rules and hazardous scenarios. Specifically, FTA analysis is performed using the knowledge from the constructed domain model to derive key objects and their environmental conditions that may lead to accidents or violations. By integrating multiple influencing factors, OntoSce can generate diverse scenarios, providing an important data foundation for the safety assessment of autonomous driving technology. We conducted experiments using the scenarios generated by OntoSce in the Apollo simulation environment, successfully identifying safety violations. This validated the feasibility and effectiveness of the generated scenarios. Additionally, the scenarios generated by OntoSce are compatible with all simulation platforms, such as CARLA, LGSVL, etc.

articleTitle: MonoDDT: Monocular 3D Object Detection Enhanced by Data-Driven Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Monocular 3D object detection is an important task in the field of computer vision, offering advantages of convenience, real-time processing, and low cost. It provides critical information for downstream tasks such as object tracking and semantic seg-mentation, and plays a significant role in applications like autono-mous driving. However, the lack of training data has become a major obstacle to improving the accuracy of this task. As a key aspect of deep learning, data-driven methods can effectively en-hance detector performance without increasing inference costs. In this paper, we propose MonoDDT, a monocular 3D object detector enhanced by data-driven techniques. By leveraging the left and right images along with the projection matrices from the KITTI dataset, we project the ground truth boxes to another viewpoint, generating auxiliary localization labels. We then identify a set of auxiliary localization labels that progressively approximate the ground truth. The DloU3D between the ground truth boxes and auxiliary localization labels is used as the auxiliary localization la-bel score. Each object with ground truth is augmented to include one object with two ground truth boxes and multiple auxiliary lo-calization labels. The approach effectively increases the training data, accelerates model convergence, and improves algorithm ac-curacy. Experimental results demonstrate that MonoDDT achieves 16.78 AP3D performance (loU=0.7, car, moderate) on the KITTI dataset, outperforming the baseline method and effectively addressing the common challenge of limited training data in mo-nocular 3D object detection.

articleTitle: Sentiment Mining and Visualization of Covid-19-Related Weibo Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly disrupted daily life worldwide, eliciting diverse emotional responses as individuals faced the uncertainties of the crisis. Social media platforms like Weibo became critical outlets for public expression, capturing a rich spectrum of sentiments that evolved with key events and policy changes. This study utilizes Weibo data to conduct fine-grained sentiment analysis, addressing the limitations of traditional models that classify emotions into broad categories (positive, negative, neutral), which fail to capture the complexity of emotions during a prolonged health crisis. By comparing the performance of three advanced NLP models-BERT-LSTM, XLNet, and RoBERTa-this research identifies BERT-LSTM as a promising candidate for detecting temporal dependencies and nuanced emotions, including fear, anger, sadness, disgust, gratitude, surprise, and optimism. Leveraging BERT-LSTM, we annotated unlabeled data to build a comprehensive dataset, which was then used to develop a dynamic visualization system. This system illustrates sentiment trends over time, offering public health officials and policymakers actionable insights into emotional responses to critical events and policy developments. By revealing emotional responses to critical events, policy changes, and health developments, the system supports data-driven decision-making and enhances understanding of public mood dynamics. The findings highlight the value of fine-grained sentiment analysis and dynamic visualization in navigating public health crises, offering a framework that can be adapted for future crises or real-time sentiment monitoring efforts.

articleTitle: Steportation: An Effective Walking-based Locomotion Method for VR
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The virtual space can often be infinite, but the user's space is always constrained. In order to mitigate the limitations of a constrained physical space to explore an infinite virtual environment, many artificial locomotion techniques have been proposed. One of the most commonly used locomotion techniques is teleportation, which allows users to explore the entire virtual environment without moving. However, this method is unnatural and can lead to spatial disorientation, lack of motion perception and sense of presence. Subsequent studies have also proposed improvements to enhance immersion of the teleportation, but the perception of motion is still distinct from that of real walking. In this paper, we introduce our method called “Steportation”, which combines natural direct walking and walking-based teleportation. The key is that users are able to trigger teleportation like natural walking and implicitly switch between teleportation and natural walking using the ‘Teleport Circle’ mechanism, eliminating the need for hand controllers. We compare our method with conventional controller-pointing teleportation, gaze teleportation and jumping teleportation, and evaluate these methods in terms of efficiency, accuracy, ease of use, and immersion through a series of experiments. The experimental results show that our method improves sense of presence and immersion while maintaining efficiency and usability.

articleTitle: Perceptual Quality-Driven Compression and Transmission of Three-Dimensional Vibrotactile Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Vibrotactile signals are one of the key cues for human to acquire information about surface texture. Compression and transmission are crucial fact of influencing the perceptual quality of vibrotactile signals, and have captured extensive attention. However, existing work focusing on the compression and transmission of one-dimensional vibrotactile signals is not applicable to three-dimensional data, due to the failure to consider the multidimensional nature of human perception. To this end, this paper proposes a compression and transmission algorithm based on three-dimensional vibrotactile signals, expanding perceptual thresholds to three-dimensional space and combining packet rate control transmission algorithms. Experimental results show that the method can effectively reduce the amount of transmitted data while maintaining the signal quality and channel stability, with a compression ratio of 60.26% at a signal quality of about 92.8.

articleTitle: Lightweight Design of the Large Arm of Palletizing Robot Based on Inspire Software
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Lightweight design has been extensively adopted in the industrial sector, significantly contributing to cost reduction, performance enhancement, and energy conservation.
