This study focuses on the large arm of a palletizing robot, employing Altair Inspire software to conduct dynamic simulation analysis, initial strength assessment, lightweight design, and subsequent strength verification. Throughout the lightweight design process, the optimal shape control scheme, quality target, and thickness parameters were determined by systematically comparing the results of various optimization analyses. A comparative study was conducted to evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of fitting PolyNURBS, adaptive geometric reconstruction, and manual geometric reconstruction. By emphasizing the reduction of stress concentration and the assurance of structural continuity, the adaptive and manual geometric reconstruction methods were selected for the lightweight design of the large arm. This approach successfully achieved a weight reduction of 69.19%. Subsequent strength analysis of the lightweight arm indicated a maximum displacement of 0.2118 mm, a minimum safety factor of 2.4, and a maximum von Mises equivalent stress of 135.5 MPa, thereby fulfilling the required strength design criteria. The study successfully reduced processing costs while ensuring the strength and stiffness of the large arm, thereby enhancing the responsiveness and reliability of the palletizing robot. Consequently, it establishes a foundational basis for the lightweight design of palletizing robots.

articleTitle: A Graph-Based Unsupervised Log Anomaly Detection Based on the Magnetic Laplacian
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Logs record the runtime status of software systems and detailed information of user operations. However, due to the complexity and heterogeneity of log formats and semantics, log anomaly detection work faces challenges. Most existing log anomaly detection methods only consider the quantitative and/or sequential relationships, while ignoring the directional information within logs, which may result in low detection accuracy. In addition, the high cost of manual annotation for logs is another challenge to effective log analysis. To address the aforementioned challenges, this paper introduces L2G-Log, a graph-based unsupervised method for log anomaly detection. The method begins by constructing logs into directed, attributed, and weighted graphs, followed by employing graph neural networks for graph-level anomaly detection. Specially, we introduce a One-Class graph convolutional neural network based on the magnetic Laplacian called OCMagNet. Firstly, it extracts the directional information in log graphs through the magnetic Laplacian and generates a vector representation for each node in graphs. Then, it utilizes Readout(·) to aggregate vector representations into a graph representation for each log graph. Finally, DeepSVDD is employed to identify anomalies without manual labeling of log data. Experiments conducted on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that L2G-Log achieves performance that is on par with or surpasses existing anomaly detection methods.

articleTitle: Industrial Energy Forecasting Using Machine Learning and Plant Activity Metrics
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: This paper reports the development of a prototype AI-driven energy forecasting tool for industrial applications, designed to operate with energy metering systems and plant activity metrics. A time history of real-time plant activity data, which is typically available from SCADA-based asset activity indicators and operational parameters, is utilised along with energy timeseries data within a model regressed to correlate energy consumption with high accuracy. Prototype software was developed as a Windows Forms application and applied to an industrial case study: provision of real-time energy forecasts and optimization insights for a working sawmill are discussed. The application has been designed for future integration with existing SCADA systems, enabling seamless, automated energy monitoring, forecasting and decision support. Future enhancements of the model include incorporating specific production types and more granular operational data to further refine prediction accuracy, and application to profiling energy efficiency of process design options. The work highlights the potential for practical and low-cost AI-powered tools to enhance energy efficiency in modern manufacturing environments and process industries, including small/medium enterprises (SMEs).

articleTitle: Lightweight Multimodal Algorithm for Automated Pain Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Pain assessment is crucial in medicine, as it indicates patient health and guides diagnosis and treatment. Traditional methods have significant limitations, especially for children, unconscious patients, and those in intensive care. Therefore, this study proposes a multimodal automated pain assessment algorithm that analyses facial expressions, vocal sounds, and variations in facial temperature. The algorithm integrates multimodal data through fusion at both the feature level and the decision level. First, it combines data from facial temperature and expressions to create a bimodal model. Then, it trains an audio model separately. The algorithm unifies these models to generate decision values that are combined into a new feature matrix for prediction. Therefore this lightweight multimodal pain assessment algorithm reduces complexity and cost while ensuring accuracy, offering broader and more effective pain management for the general public.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Generative AI in E-commerce Product Description Generation: An Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Generative AI has emerged as a powerful tool for content generation in e-commerce, enabling the automated creation of product descriptions, reviews, and marketing copy. This paper presents a systematic evaluation of state-of-the-art generative AI models for e-commerce content generation using the WANDS dataset. We conduct a series of experiments to compare commonly used AI models based on their BLEU and ROUGE scores, assessing their effectiveness in generating high-quality, coherent, and contextually relevant content. Our analysis reveals distinct strengths for each model: GPT-4 excels in producing high-conversion SEO-driven sales copy, Claude generates engaging, storytelling-rich product descriptions, DeepSeek provides precise, factual descriptions for technical products, LLaMA offers simple, cost-effective product descriptions, and OpenHermes-2.5-Mistral-7B creates engaging and informative product descriptions suitable for e-commerce platforms. These findings highlight the importance of aligning AI model selection with specific e-commerce use cases and content objectives. By providing a comprehensive benchmark and targeted recommendations, this study offers valuable insights for businesses and researchers seeking to optimize AI-driven content generation strategies in online retail, enabling more effective and tailored implementation of generative AI in e-commerce contexts.

articleTitle: A Software Defect Prediction Model Enhanced by Self-Attention Mechanism and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Software defect prediction is a key aspect of software quality assurance that involves the use of historical data and a variety of analytical techniques to estimate which parts of the code are most likely to contain errors. Not only can software defects lead to system failure, but they can also have serious economic and social consequences. Most of the current methods rely on a single type of feature and fail to explore the multiple information in the code fully. Meanwhile, manually tuning hyperparameters is both time-consuming and difficult to achieve optimal results. Based on the encoder architecture, this research proposes an enhanced software defect prediction model, which combines the self-attention mechanism and particle swarm optimization (PSO-BiEncoders-SelfAttn). This model achieves efficient feature extraction, dynamic adjustment of feature fusion weights, and automated optimization of hyperparameters. This study trained and tested the model on five different publicly available datasets and evaluated it using metrics including precision, recall, and F-measure. The proposed PSO-BiEncoders-SelfAttn model improves the state-of-art, achieving an average F-measure improvement of 7.92% according to the experimental result.

articleTitle: Visualizing Credit Default Risk: Insights Through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: We apply machine learning to predict credit default risk, aiming to enhance the accuracy of financial risk assessment models and provide valuable insights for risk management. Post-pandemic economic challenges and rising loan defaults have caused significant losses for financial institutions. Existing models fail to deliver sufficient accuracy, and we address this gap by leveraging advanced machine-learning techniques. We design a machine-learning pipeline to analyze and predict credit default risk. We test models like XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, and Deep Neural Networks. We improve performance through feature engineering and optimize models using random search. By combining XGBoost, LightGBM, and Random Forest into an ensemble, we achieve further enhancements. Our final model reaches an AUC of 0.784, proving its effectiveness and laying the groundwork for future advancements in financial risk management.

articleTitle: Multi-Relation Graph Transformer and Edge Aware Learning: A Scalable Approach for Detecting Fraud in Heterogeneous Graphs
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Detecting fraud in multi-relational graphs is a significant difficulty due to the complex nature of fraudulent activities and the inadequacies of conventional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in managing heterophilic relationships and long-range dependencies. Current GNN-based models experience over-smoothing and over-squashing, which constrains their capacity to differentiate between fraudulent and legitimate interactions. To tackle these difficulties, we offer MR-GT, a Graph Transformer-based model that integrates multi-relational attention and edge-aware techniques to enhance fraud detection. MR-GT implements edge-aware message passing and edge-based attention bias, enabling the model to concentrate on significant transactional links while disregarding less pertinent interactions. The approach utilizes relation-aware aggregation to accurately identify fraud-related patterns in diverse interactions. Experimental findings on the Yelp and Amazon datasets indicate that MR-GT significantly surpasses state-of-the-art approaches, attaining an AVC of 92.33 on Yelp and 98.25 on Amazon. The ablation study further illustrates the significance of each component, indicating that MR-GT provides a scalable and efficient approach for identifying fraud in extensive, multi-relational graphs.

articleTitle: Voiceprint Diagnosis Method for Urban Rail Power Transformers Based on Mel Spectrogram and Improved Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The fault diagnosis for urban rail power transformers is crucial for ensuring the safety and reliability of urban rail power systems. Voiceprint-based fault diagnosis methods have gradually become a research hotspot due to their non-contact and uninterrupted advantages, especially with significant progress in the application of deep learning methods in this field. However, challenges such as poor robustness against noise interference and scarcity of real fault samples still persist. Therefore, this paper proposes a voiceprint diagnosis method for urban rail power transformers based on Mel spectrogram and an improved Vision Transformer(ViT). The improved ViT model integrates a CNN encoder and adopts a column-wise patch strategy, building upon the original ViT architecture. Experimental results show that the proposed method, with only 0.47M parameters and 0.149GLOPs, achieves a mere 6.75% accuracy drop when the signal-to-noise ratio decreases from 10dB to -4dB, outperforming other comparative methods.

articleTitle: Intelligent Identification of Airborne Target Trajectory Behaviour Based on Long Time-Series Space-Based Radar Data
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: As the intensity of confrontation in the neighbourhood continues to escalate, the air defence threat facing our country is growing, and information-based air defence is facing unprecedented challenges. On the basis of existing aviation detection means, comprehensive analysis of airborne targets is the primary task of exploring the laws of information-based air defence. Among them, the civil-military identification of flying targets is crucial to the military's operational decision-making and battlefield control. Hence, this study focuses on trajectory signal processing, machine learning intelligent recognition based on manual sequence features, and improvement of TSFRESH feature extraction to enhance its timeliness. Specifically, we design a rule-based filtering method to effectively remove wild-value data from the original trajectory data. And then we propose a support vector machine model based on manual sequence features. Effective trajectory features are extracted based on TSFRESH, and the support vector machine model is used to achieve the classification of military and civilian aircraft. Meanwhile to shorten the TSFRESH feature extraction time, we use the mutual information method to downscale the extracted features to speed up the classification time. Experiments show that this method can achieve the task of classifying military and civilian aircraft based on trajectory information and significantly reduce the running time.

articleTitle: Hybird Clustering Algorithm Based on BP Neural Network and K-means
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In the era of big data, efficient and accurate clustering algorithms are indispensable for organizing and mining information. This paper focuses on the optimization of clustering algorithms, particularly by integrating the advantages of the Backpropagation (BP) neural network and the K-means algorithm to enhance clustering accuracy and stability. This paper proposed improvement strategy introduces a novel fusion method that combines the self-learning characteristic of the BP neural network with the crowd wisdom of the K-means algorithm, resulting in a hybrid model that dynamically adjusts cluster centroids. In this model, the BP network is responsible for generating and updating initial cluster centroids, while the K-means algorithm allocates samples based on these centroids. This complementary approach forms an iterative optimization process. The aim is to address the limitations of traditional K-means when dealing with complex data structures and the initialization challenge faced by the BP network in clustering tasks. The implementation section involves programming the improved algorithm using the sklearn library and testing it on the classic iris dataset. Through comparisons with the original K-means algorithm and clustering solely with the BP neural network,this demonstrates the superiority of the improved algorithm in clustering performance.

articleTitle: SNN-GST: Gradient-Based Security Testing Method for Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have garnered significant attention in the field of deep learning due to their efficient energy utilization and inspiration drawn from neuroscience. However, the security issues of SNNs, particularly their vulnerability in safety-critical tasks, have attracted the attention of researchers. Therefore, we have investigated the security issues of SNNs and designed a security testing method for SNNs, termed SNN-GST. This method leverages an understanding of the working principles and vulnerabilities of SNNs to conduct gradient-based adversarial attacks. It employs gradient optimization techniques to find solutions and adjusts the spiking threshold to reduce ineffective spikes. Additionally, it introduces a perturbation norm constraint method to decrease the average perturbation required for the attack. Furthermore, we have designed a method and metrics for evaluating the temporal robustness of SNNs. By integrating the SNN-GST method for conducting attack tests, we have assessed the robustness of the models across various datasets. This study aims to design the SNN-GST for a comprehensive quantitative assessment of the robustness of SNNs, providing scientific methods and metrics to enhance their security, and ensuring the reliability of SNNs in practical applications.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Intelligent Periodic Table of Elements Based on FBS-Agent
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The Periodic Table of Elements (PTE) is a manifestation of the periodic system of elements, containing a large number of physical and chemical laws of elements, which can be used to PTE and guide the design of compounds. However, the existing software systems for PTE generally lack intelligent characteristics and require familiarity with element properties and relationships in order to effectively utilize them. We design Structure-Function-Behavior-based Agent (FBS-Agent) model for chemical element in this article. The intelligent PTE software system was implemented based on FBS-Agent, which can conveniently retrieval the atomic structure, chemical properties, and physical properties of different elements in the periodic system of elements. On the basis of the periodic law of elements, the software system adopts artificial intelligence and chemical big data to achieve the retrieval, comparison, and analysis of different properties of elements and element groups; By utilizing the compound knowledge and rules of known elements, the software system can intelligently recommend and discover potential compound information. The intelligent retrieval and automatic recommendation functions of this system are active attempts of AI4R (Artificial Intelligence for Research) in exploration of chemical mechanisms. The design of the software system has important teaching and guidance significance for learning, mastering, and utilizing the properties of chemical elements, which will further promote the interdisciplinary integration of ChemAI (Chemistry and Artificial Intelligence).

articleTitle: Concept-wise Feature Sampling: Mitigating Object Hallucinations for Large Vision-Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have advanced significantly due to the integration of multimodal data, enabling improved performance across various applications. However, the persistent challenge of hallucination-where models generate plausible but inaccurate content-remains a significant barrier to their practical deployment, particularly in critical fields such as healthcare and autonomous driving. This paper presents a concept-wise feature sampling (CFS) framework that addresses object hallucination by leveraging the strengths of existing pixel-level and feature-level approaches. By utilizing CLIP components to identify relevant object concepts and employing a semantic segmentation model (Mask CLIP) to sample least similar features, our method enhances the visual interpretability of predictions while maintaining computational efficiency. Rigorous evaluations on standard benchmarks show that CFS effectively reduces object hallucinations in LVLMs and supports a more explainable flow of suboptimal multimodal information, paving the way for safer applications of these models.

articleTitle: A Novel Trend-Pattern Unlimited Fuzzy Information Granule-Based Long-Term Forecasting Model for Multivariate Time Series
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Long-term forecasting of multivariate time series (MTS) is a crucial yet challenging task due to the intricate interdependencies among variables and the error accumulation over long-term timesteps. Facing with this challenging task, trend fuzzy information granulation has been recognized as an effective approach achieving substantial research outcomes. By transforming numerical time series into granular time series, it captures the trend information in data and effectively alleviates the error accumulation in long-term forecasting. However, existing trend fuzzy information granulation methods typically assume that the trend variations conform to predefined patterns, which limits their ability to accurately model the nonlinear trends presented in real-world MTS data. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a trend-pattern unlimited fuzzy information granulation (TUFIG) method for MTS. Unlike traditional methods, TUFIG can adaptively learn trend representations from data without prior assumptions of trend morphology, thereby modeling the nonlinear trends more flexibly. In order to capture the temporal and spatial correlations in the multivariate granular time series transformed from the original time series, we further design a two-stage attention mechanism (TAM). Based on the proposed granulation method and TAM, we develop a long-term forecasting model for MTS. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets show that the proposed forecasting model significantly outperforms existing mainstream methods in forecasting accuracy, showcasing substantial application potential. This research not only provides an innovative solution for multivariate time series forecasting but also offers theoretical support for enhancing forecasting accuracy in practical applications.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Online Log Parsing Method Based on ALBERT and K-Means ++ Clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Log resolution is a method to convert unstructured or semi-structured log data into structured log templates. It is often used as an intermediate link to serve downstream tasks such as log anomaly detection. In view of the log management statistics and abnormal information search requirements of the operation monitoring of the ground system of Fengyun 4B satellite, it is difficult for existing methods to analyze the logs of complex structure with high accuracy. This paper takes the logs of planning and scheduling software and equipment monitoring software as the research object, and proposes an analysis method that can adapt to the logs of complex structure and generate a log template to provide an overview of automatic online log analysis. In this method, a preprocessing process is designed to improve the generalization, and the ALBERT model, PCA dimensionality reduction method and K-Means ++ clustering method are used to improve the efficiency while ensuring the accuracy. The method is applied to the open source HDFS data set and the software log data set of Fengyun 4B satellite ground system, and both the accurate analyses is more than 99%. The analysis results of this method and existing analytical methods applied to the log data set of monitoring software show that the accuracy of this analytical method is improved to 15%, and the running time is shortened by more than 70%, which is the best analytical method. Therefore, this method is an effective method for analyzing complex engineering logs with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Personalized Book Recommendation Engine with Emotional Understanding and Contextual Relevance Based on Hybrid Filtering - A Novel Method Providing Recommendation Explanation
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel personalized book recommendation system that integrates emotional understanding and contextual relevance to enhance the accuracy and personalization of suggestions. The system employs a hybrid filtering method, combining content-based and collaborative filtering, to address the limitations of traditional recommendation systems. By incorporating Explainable AI (XAI), the system provides transparent justifications for each recommendation, enhancing user trust and engagement. Additionally, sentiment analysis and contextual factors, such as weather, time of day, and the user's emotional state, are considered to ensure that the recommended books align with the user's current circumstances. Our findings show that the integration of Explainable AI significantly improved user satisfaction and engagement. Testing with 100 participants resulted in a high level of satisfaction, with 55% reporting that they found the recommendations more trustworthy due to explanations. The system makes a significant contribution to improving emotional well-being by providing personalized recommendations.

articleTitle: Advanced Deep Learning Techniques for Lung Sound Classification: Binary, Multi-Class, and Ensemble Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Detecting respiratory diseases, particularly lung disorders is crucial due to their global prevalence. Auscultation by experts has been the standard method for detecting lung diseases. However, the efficiency of diagnosis can be greatly increased by automating this procedure. Using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for binary classification and a CNN, CNN-LSTM hybrid model for multi class classification, this study uses deep learning approaches to automate lung sound classification. To increase classification accuracy, the study extracts important elements from lung sounds such as chromograms, Mel spectrograms and Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). Ensemble learning which combines CNN and CNN-LSTM for multi-class classification, substantially improves the model. With an accuracy of 86.11% the suggested ensemble model surpasses current models in the field. The accuracy of binary classification is 88.38%. This study demonstrates the advantages of combining multiple architectures to improve classification performance and shows how deep learning models can be used to effectively classify lung sounds. The results have significant implications for the early detection of lung diseases.

articleTitle: Graph Convolutional Networks with Dynamic Subgraph Sampling for Recommendation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Graph neural networks provide a powerful frame-work for recommendation systems by capturing dependencies through message passing and modeling user-item interactions using an adjacency matrix. However, as the number of users and items increases, the adj acency matrix grows larger and sparser, leading to an over-reliance on the existing graph structure. These challenges require frequent retraining, which ultimately restricts scalability and diminishes recommendation performance. This pa-per presents a recommendation algorithm of dynamic sub-graph sampling to address the challenges of data sparsity and graph de-pendency in recommendation systems based on graph neural net-works. The proposed algorithm alleviates data sparsity and graph dependency issues by dynamically sampling subgraphs to estab-lish adaptive user-item interactions by shifting from traditional whole-graph training to subgraph-based training. The proposed approach enhances aggregation and sampling techniques, proving the efficacy of separate subgraph sampling for user and item nodes. Its effectiveness is validated through comparative, ablation, and hyperparameter experiments across multiple benchmark datasets, outperforming baselines consistently.

articleTitle: Design Matrix Factorization and Knowledge-Guided Clustering for Trust-Aware Cross-Domain Recommendation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The core challenge in designing an algorithm for trust-aware cross-domain recommendation systems lies in effectively integrating ratings from all domains (target-domain and source-domains) and trust relationships to improve recommendation performance in the target-domain. These systems involve two types of information fusion: intra-domain information fusion, which integrates intra-domain trust relationships and ratings within each domain (target-domain or source-domain), and cross-domain information fusion, which fuses information from all domains through inter-domain trust relationships as a bridge. The existing algorithms are limited in that they only address either intra-domain information fusion or cross-domain information fusion, failing to comprehensively utilize both intra-domain and inter-domain trust relationships for integrating information from all domains. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach that combines inter-domain information fusion and cross-domain information fusion. Based on this approach, we design a matrix factorization and knowledge-guided clustering based trust-aware cross-domain collaborative filtering algorithm (MFKC _ TCCFA). Experimental results on a dataset show that MFKC_TCCFA outperforms existing state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Multi-Model Fusion for Analyzing Staircase Wear and Human Traffic Patterns
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: This paper aims at providing scientific guideline for archaeological research by analyzing the relationship between stair wear and human activity patterns. The Archard Model is adopted to build staircase wear model to take account of human activities and natural influences. A Dynamic Wear Differential Equation is derived and the Numerical stability is ensured by spatial and temporal discretization, explicit Eulerian and CFL conditions. The maximum, minimum and average wear depth are 1.5568 mm, 0.0668 mm and 0.3452 mm, respectively, which is consistent with the assumptions of human activity habits and Gaussian distribution of pedestrian flow. A Multi-Source Information Fusion Model, which employs a simplified Archard wear equation, is constructed to predict human activity patterns. A Gradient Boosted Decision Tree (GBDT) was applied to fit the model, and 5-fold cross-validation and Bayesian optimization were used to improve the prediction accuracy. The usage frequency of the stair can be estimated as 493 persons/day. To predict the walk direction and pattern, the longitudinal and lateral features are defined, and the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) and Bayesian Classification Framework are applied. The obtained results show that the peak spacing: 0.39 m and the asymmetry index: 0.10. A Multi-Angle Analysis of Measurement Model is proposed to optimize the measurement data collection. The sampling density function, error evaluation model and time measurement model are established and solved iteratively. The results exhibit high accuracy with average measurement error of 0.003 mm and total measurement time of 421.55 hours, which indicates the data obtained by the proposed measurement scheme is reliable for the subsequent analysis. To realize the time series reconstruction of the staircase by the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method, the Bayesian Temporal Inference Model and Multi-information Historical Reconstruction Model are developed. The factors which have great influence on the staircase wear are considered including the intensity of use, environmental impacts, and maintenance activities. To validate the proposed model and method, and the given dataset is adopted. The age of the staircase is estimated to be about 219.2 years, with an error no more than 40 years. The model was also effective in analyzing the reliability of the renovation, material sources, and historical records with a reliability index of 0.8. The sensitivity analysis is performed to quantify the prediction error using Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Compared with the impact of human activity intensity and path distribution standard deviation, the diffusion coefficient has a greater impact on the accuracy of predicting the frequency of stair use.

articleTitle: System for Automating Medication Orders to the Hospital Pharmacy by Nurses in Peru Through Voice Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The management of nurses' orders to a Peruvian hospital pharmacy faces efficiency challenges, which affects time spent on patient care. This context highlights the need for a system that optimizes this process. In this sense, a web-based system is proposed for the automation of orders from the nurse's cell phone, which uses a customized model for automatic speech recognition. The development of the system was divided into three stages: first, data collection with 21 orders placed by three nurses and 978 audio recordings to validate the automatic speech recognition model; second, implementation of the system allowing agile order processing; and finally, evaluation of results in terms of time and accuracy. The findings indicate that the processing time ranged from 37.70 to 60.15 seconds, representing a 97%-time reduction in operational tasks. In addition, the Word Error Rate was 10.51%, significantly lower than the 25.05% of Whisper Large V2. These results demonstrate the system's potential for adoption in various hospital contexts.

articleTitle: Semi-Dense Scene Reconstruction Based on Stereo Event Cameras
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Compared to standard cameras, event cameras that work asynchronously offer many advantages, such as low power consumption, high temporal resolution, and high dynamic range, making them valuable tools for tasks like real-time 3D reconstruction, simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), and more. However, due to the asynchronous event output characteristic and their photometric sensing method, traditional 3D reconstruction algorithms are challenging to apply directly. Existing reconstruction methods based on stereo event cameras often face issues such as pose estimation drift and insufficient reconstruction accuracy in complex motion scenarios. To address this, this paper builds a semi-dense 3D reconstruction system based on stereo event cameras, comprehensively compares four commonly used event stream processing methods, and proposes an innovative event representation method Adaptive Time Surface. This method uses an exponential decay kernel to convert event streams into distance field-like event image frames, allowing adaptive parameter adjustment to accommodate differ-ent event frequencies, thereby generating event representations with stable brightness. This significantly enhances the robustness of pose estimation and the accuracy of scene reconstruction. Extensive experiments in real-world scenarios validate that the 3D reconstruction system based on ATS demonstrates stronger robustness and higher accuracy in camera pose estimation and scene reconstruction compared to other event stream processing methods.

articleTitle: Spatial and Temporal Analysis in High-Quality Development Level of Shandong Province
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In the context of China's economic transformation and upgrading and regional coordinated development strategy, Shandong Province, as an important region in the Yellow River Basin, its high-quality development level is significant to promoting regional economic growth and achieving sustainable development. The focus of this study is to (1) establish a high-quality development evaluation index system based on five dimensions: innovation, coordination, sharing, greenness, and openness; (2) apply the entropy weight method to evaluate the high-quality development level of Shandong Province from 2008 to 2022; (3) analyze the difference and correlation of high-quality coordinated development among 17 cities in Shandong Province from 2009 to 2022. The finding suggests Shandong Province has achieved outstanding performance and progress in the high-quality development of innovation, sharing, and greenness dimensions while needing to improve in coordinated and openness dimensions. The high-quality coordinated development of 17 cities in Shan dong Province reflects spatial differences and an aggregation effect, showing that most inland cities gather in cold spot areas with low development levels. The study concludes by offering implications for the future high-quality and coordinated development of Shandong Province based on the insights gained from the analysis.

articleTitle: Unveiling Travel Trends in Turkey: A Visual Analysis of Social Network Data
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: We analyze the importance of nodes and community structures within Turkey's tourism network to optimize resource allocation and improve strategic decision-making. With the rapid growth of global tourism, understanding the structure and dynamics of tourism networks is crucial for effective resource management and revenue optimization. Turkey serves as an ideal case study due to its unique geographic location bridging Europe and Asia, its rich cultural heritage, and its diverse tourist attractions, which draw visitors from various regions. However, Turkey's tourism sector faces significant challenges, including seasonal fluctuations, changing visitor demographics, and sensitivity to political events. Addressing these issues is essential for ensuring sustainable tourism development. To address these challenges, we apply social network analysis and compare the performance of five community detection algorithms to identify the most effective model for analyzing Turkey's tourism network. Our results show that key tourist hubs, such as Ephesus Ancient City, the Bosphorus Strait, and Pergamon, serve as critical nodes within the network. We identify seasonal patterns, with visitors primarily coming from Europe, the CIS, and Asia, and highlight the impact of political events on tourism revenue. We also propose strategies such as precision marketing during peak seasons and leveraging exchange rate advantages to help improve income. Additionally, we developed a tourism social platform that uses high-impact nodes and community collaboration to enhance promotion efforts and support coordinated tourism development.

articleTitle: Advancements in Order Independent Transparency: A Survey for Real-Time Rendering Practitioners
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Order Independent Transparency (OIT) remains a pivotal challenge in real-time rendering, with applications spanning gaming, simulations, and AR/VR experiences. Traditional techniques, such as Depth Peeling and K-Buffer OIT, have provided foundational solutions to this challenge, while modern approaches like Stochastic Alpha Blending, Weighted OIT with Multi-Frustum, and Deep Learning-Based OIT have introduced innovative pathways to achieve high-quality transparency with improved performance. This survey presents a comprehensive review of these techniques, highlighting their underlying principles, implementation nuances, and trade-offs in terms of performance, memory overhead, and visual fidelity. In addition, this survey examines advanced concepts that push the boundaries of OIT, addressing the growing demands of real-time applications. By providing a detailed analysis of these methods and their suitability for various rendering contexts, this paper aims to serve as a practical guide for researchers and practitioners striving for advancements in real-time transparency solutions.

articleTitle: YOLO_MIC3: Facial Keypoints Detection Algorithm for Aggregating Reduced-Dimensional MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Clinical diagnosis and treatment are highly dependent on medical images. However, the MRI reconstruction model of the human head is limited by insufficient resolution, blurred tissue contours, and spatial impurities, which makes it difficult to accurately locate the key points of the face, and thus severely restricts its wide application in clinical scenarios. In this study, we take a unique approach to capture the MRI reconstruction model with dimensionality reduction, and construct the YOLO_MIC3 deep learning algorithm based on YOLOv8 for the obtained 2D images. Through a series of optimization strategies, such as introducing the CBAM mechanism, replacing the DarknetBottleneck component in C2f with the CAA module, and applying the Inner-CloU computational loss, the comprehensive performance of the model is improved. Experimentally, the algorithm reduces the model complexity by 25%, improves the computational efficiency by 29%, and performs well in the Box metrics dimension of mAP50-95, which provides a promising solution for the localization of clinical facial keypoints.

articleTitle: Fine-Grained Chinese Multimodal Image-Text Retrieval: A Fine Feature Alignment Method Based on CNCLIP
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: This study proposes the Chinese Fine Alignment in Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CFA-CLIP), a fine-grained feature alignment model based on Chinese Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CNCLIP), to enhance image-text retrieval performance. The method incorporates three components: (1) a data layer that uses a large language model (LLM) for sentence transformations to increase data diversity while preserving semantics; (2) a feature fusion layer that integrates local features of Masked Autoencoders (MAE) and BERT within CNCLIP's dual-stream framework for improved alignment; and (3) an auxiliary loss layer applying multi-stage contrastive learning and optimizing Image-Text Matching (ITM) loss for hard sample training. Experiments on the MUGE and Flickr30K-CN datasets show that CFA-CLIP achieves significant improvements, particularly in fine-grained retrieval.

articleTitle: The Application of Social Media in College English Teaching: Data Analysis and Visualization Research
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In the era of fragmented learning, using social media for English learning has become mainstream. College English teaching requires continuous understanding of students' online and offline learning situations and needs. Information such as the English learning topics discussed by students on social media and the areas of learning they focus on will provide important references for teachers in planning teaching and selecting teaching cases. This paper collects relevant college student English topic information from the Weibo platform and applies the GPU-DMM (Graphic Processing Unit-Dirichlet Multinomial Mixtures) semantically enhanced topic model to perform topic mining on English topics. It obtains the corresponding document-topic distribution and topic-word distribution, analyzes the differences between different topics, and identifies the focus points of college students in English learning. Finally, the information of different topics is visually displayed to systematically reflect the topical characteristics of college student English discussions.

articleTitle: Data Quality-Aware Federated Learning for Fake Review Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Fake reviews are a significant challenge for online consumer and social media platforms, as they mislead consumers and disrupt fair market competition. Traditional centralized detection methods face numerous limitations in handling massive data volumes, heterogeneous distributions, and privacy compliance. To address these issues, this paper proposes a data quality-aware federated learning framework for efficiently detecting fake reviews while preserving the privacy of data holders. Specifically, we introduce a data quality evaluation module during the federated learning training process. This module quantifies the quality of each client's data based on multiple metrics, including annotation accuracy, textual completeness, and user behavior. Higher-quality data clients are assigned greater weights during global model aggregation, thereby mitigating the interference of low-quality or noisy data. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to traditional federated averaging and other baseline methods, our approach significantly improves accuracy, precision, and recall. Additionally, it exhibits greater robustness and faster convergence under various non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) and multi-noise scenarios. Furthermore, differential privacy ensures the security of participants' raw data and quality evaluation information, enhancing the feasibility of real-world deployment.

articleTitle: RenderMiner: Mining Micro-Architecture Characteristics of Rendering Programs on GPGPU
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In recent years, page-table the applications of virtual reality, augmented reality and mixed reality have become more and more popular, all of which are essentially image rendering. Graphics rendering requires a lot of calculations to determine the rendering parameters of each pixel. However, how to reveal the micro-architecture characteristics of GPGPU to help architects increase optimization opportunities and improve the performance of microprocessors becomes imperative. In this article, we propose RenderMiner, a framework which comprehensively characterizes the GPGPU rendering programs at the instruction and memory levels. Specifically, we design instruction mix based on the SASS instruction set, instruction frequency, register reuse distribution and memory call stack to efficiently depict the micro-architecture characteristics of rendering programs and compare with the non-rendering programs. We use RenderMiner to analyze the inherent behaviors of rendering programs combined with machining learning methods through 60 CPU rendering programs, 34 GPU rendering programs, 52 GPU non-rendering programs such as Rodinia and Parboil, and some real-world workloads, such as V-Ray5 Benchmark, Blender, Octane and Kobra Vulkan. After analysis of the rendering programs and comparison with non-rendering programs and the real-world workloads, the key findings of our conclusion are as following: (1) The instruction mix of CPU rendering programs is totally different from that of MiBench, especially at the aspect of arithmetic operation, memory read, memory write and control flow. (2) The instruction-level parallel interval of the CPU rendering program is mainly concentrated from 3 to 6. (3) There is comparable instruction frequency among GPU rendering, Octane, Kobra vulkan and non-rendering programs. (4) The average total instruction count of GPU rendering programs is 355 times more than that of non-rendering programs. (5) The portion of floating point of GPU rendering programs, Blender, V-ray5 benchmark and Kobra vulkan is two times more than that of GPU non-rendering programs.

articleTitle: A Novel Sky-Aware Dehazing Approach for Outdoor Autonomous Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Clear outdoor images are essential for autonomous driving and accurate target detection, especially in haze. The majority of algorithms are unable to adequately address the issue of dehazing, resulting in a range of distortions, particularly in the sky area. This paper proposes an advanced dehazing algorithm for enhancing sky-area visuals (ESV). We segment the image into sky and non-sky areas, with atmospheric light levels being determined within the sky area. To enhance the recovery of the sky region, we suggest fine-tuning the sky's transmission to a predetermined constant value. Ultimately, the dehazed image is retrieved utilizing the atmospheric scattering model. Extensive experiments have shown that our proposed algorithm outperforms alternative methods, increasing PSNR by up to 1.3733%, 1.6360%, 2.4169%, 0.9512%, SSIM by up to 4.8995%, 0.6281%, 6.5335%, 8.7165%, enhancing the visuals of sky-area, compared to DCP, CAP, HC-CEP and AOD-Net.

articleTitle: Profiler: An Exploration of Micro-Architecture-Oblivious GPU Program Characteristics Profiling and Analysis Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Given the swift advancements in GPU architectures, the process of assessing and improving GPU rendering performance has grown increasingly sophisticated and vital. To address these challenges and provide microarchitecture-agnostic insights, this paper introduces MICPAT, a tool for GPU characteristic profiling. MICPAT extracts key program characteristics such as instruction composition, basic block count, instruction frequency and memory allocation size across NVIDIA's Kepler, Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta GPU series. By analyzing these microarchitecture-agnostic characteristics, developers gain deep insights into the behavior and performance of their GPU programs. MICPAT supports precompiled applications utilizing CUDA, OpenACC, OpenCL, or CUDA Fortran. Serving as a versatile platform, MICPAT enables consistent analysis across this diverse set of GPU architectures and precompiled application environments. Utilizing Octane renderer, as well as Rodinia and Parboil benchmarks, extensive experimental evaluations across 100 GPU rendering applications have validated MICPAT's efficacy and its microarchitecture-agnostic nature. The open source repo is https://zenodo.org/records/13623324.

articleTitle: TLFIG-Transformer: Trend-Oriented Linear Fuzzy Information Granulation-Based Transformer Model for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Long-term time series forecasting holds significant practical value in various fields. However, time series data exhibit complex dynamic characteristics, including trends, seasonality, and noise. These features pose substantial challenges for long-term forecasting. This paper proposes a trend-oriented fuzzy information granulation method and combines it with Transformers to construct a long-term time series forecasting model. By performing decomposition on the time series, the model can extract core trend information and apply fuzzy granulation to it, reducing the influence of other interfering factors on the forecasting process. To better capture long-term dependencies in time series data, this paper designs multiple Transformer modules. Some of these modules are designed to process trend information at the granular level, while others model additional features at the numerical level. This architecture adopts a direct multi-step forecasting strategy, avoiding the error accumulation issue commonly found in traditional autoregressive models. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model offers significant advantages in improving forecasting accuracy, handling complex dynamic changes, and enhancing computational efficiency. By integrating trend information granulation with deep learning models, this paper presents an innovative and efficient solution for long-term time series forecasting tasks.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Integration of Educational Resources and Intelligent Questions and Answers Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: This research presents an innovative educational resource integration and intelligent Questions and Answers (Q&A) system for Sichuan University-Pittsburgh Institute (SCUPI), combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology with Large Language Models (LLMs). Through controlled experiments with admission-related queries, our system demonstrates significant advantages over baseline models in three aspects: response accuracy through knowledge integration, information boundary management, and contextual awareness in multi-turn conversations. The findings provide valuable insights for implementing AI consultation systems in international higher education programs, particularly in managing admission inquiries.

articleTitle: DeepSD:Sinkhorn Distance Calculated by Different Methods for Few-Shot Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Few-Shot Learning (FSL) has emerged as an effective approach for tasks with limited or no labeled samples, showing great potential. However, the challenge remains in efficiently extracting and learning valuable information in a timely manner. In this study, we revisit Few-Shot Learning classification methods from an optimization perspective. We leverage the Sinkhorn Distance (SD) as a measure of similarity between computationally intensive sample features. Moreover, we explore the Sinkhorn Stabilized Distance (SSD) and Unbalanced Sinkhorn Distance (UNSD) to optimize the matching flow between two samples, aiming for the best alignment. To address issues stemming from intra-class variations and the challenge of differentiating foreground and background features, we introduce the Polarized Selective Kernel Attention (PSKA) mechanism. Extensive experiments validate the efficacy of our proposed methods, demonstrating competitive performance across multiple benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Visual Translation of Urban Rental Research Based on Beishan Village in Guangzhou from the Perspective of Communication Studies
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The city functions as a medium formed by its public, with the life experiences and identity dissemination of young creative groups serving as a manifestation of urban soft power. This study, grounded in the theoretical development of communication studies and the practice of visual translation, constructs a triadic theoretical framework of “spatial-cognitive-semiotic” dimensions. Integrating sociological empirical research with digital visual technologies employs visual translation to interpret and present social research on urban rental housing. This study proposes and implements an action pathway consisting of the following steps: language-mediated in-depth interviews, media-assisted information expression and storage, data modeling of emotions and attitudes, computer vision-driven symbolic decoding and semantic translation, and visual re-dissemination of research findings. By leveraging digital tools, this study seeks to enhance media communication efficiency and facilitate social interaction among heterogeneous individuals, reinforcing the emotional connection between young people and urban spaces while fostering the deep integration of communication practices and social governance.

articleTitle: Explainable Feature Selection Based on Feature Importance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 7th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Feature selection plays a significant role in reducing the curse of dimensionality and enhancing the performance of deep learning models. To address the shortcomings of existing feature selection techniques in handling complex correlations between features and their lack of explainability, we propose an explainable feature selection method based on feature importance analysis, called FeatureImp. The method evaluates the contribution of features to model predictions through feature perturbation and uses statistical analysis methods to determine the relationships between different features and the potential associations between features and labels. It further identifies combinations of multiple features that may significantly impact the prediction results, thereby optimizing the feature contribution values by simultaneously perturbing multiple features. During the feature selection process, the optimal feature subset is determined based on the feature contribution values and correlation coefficients. Different from existing feature selection methods, FeatureImp quantifies the contribution of features to the model and is applicable to all types of model architectures. We apply FeatureImp to eight public datasets with varying feature dimensions using four types of deep learning models. The results show that FeatureImp reduces the number of features by an average of 30.57%. When models are trained and tested using the datasets after feature selection, the performance of 81.25 % of the models is improved. In addition, FeatureImp is compared with the existing feature selection techniques, the F-measure is increased by an average of 1.57%, and the MAE is decreased by an average of 5.07 %, which validates the effectiveness of FeatureImp.
